# Architecture — planr dashboard (SPEC-016)

## Overview

The dashboard is a Node-ESM, zero-npm-runtime-dependency server that serves a
single-page client application. It is deliberately **not** a typical web
application framework: it is a plugin component that reuses the existing board
daemon infrastructure (`lib/design-engine/daemon.mjs`) and extends it with
dashboard-specific routes and a filesystem watcher.

## File map

```

  server.mjs              HTTP server — all routes, SSE client set, in-memory graph cache, watcher start/stop
  graph-engine.mjs        Delegate-or-fallback orchestrator (A.1 CLI, A.2 native reader)
  graph-reader.mjs        Native .planr/ frontmatter reader (A.2 path)
  watcher.mjs             .planr/ filesystem observer, debouncer, diff engine, SSE patch emitter
  vendor/
    graph-layout.js       Self-contained layered-DAG layout engine (zero external deps)
```

## Data flow

```
/planr-pipeline:dashboard (agent invocation)
        |
        v
commands/dashboard.md  →  procedures/dashboard-preflight.md
        |  (resolve port, mode, reuse-or-start)
        v
lib/dashboard/server.mjs  — createDashboardServer({ planrDir, watch })
        |
        |── GET /api/graph ──→ graph-engine.mjs:buildGraph(planrDir)
        |                            |
        |                            |── A.1: planr graph --json  (CLI, if >= v1.7.2)
        |                            |       → validateJson → return
        |                            └── A.2: graph-reader.mjs:readGraph(planrDir)
        |                                      → walkArtifacts → parseFrontmatter
        |                                      → inferType / classifyStatus
        |                                      → buildEdges → validateJson → return
        |
        |── GET /api/node/:id ──→ graph-engine.mjs:getNode → graph-reader.mjs:readNode
        |                         (always native: body text is not in CLI output)
        |
        |── GET /api/events ──→ SSE stream; broadcasts watcher patches to all clients
        |
        |── GET /api/meta ──→ { version, planrDir, views, defaultView }
        |
        |── GET /health ──→ { ok, pid }   (reuse-if-running probe)
        |
        └── GET /* ──→ static file from lib/dashboard/app/ (traversal-guarded)

lib/dashboard/watcher.mjs  (runs if --no-watch is absent)
        |
        |── fs.watch('.planr/', { recursive: true }) or polling fallback
        |── debounce 300ms
        |── buildGraph(planrDir, { scope: changedId })
        |── diffGraphs(snapshot, next) → patch { updated, added, removed, edges }
        └── onPatch(patch) → server broadcasts to sseClients → client mergePatch()
```

## Key design decisions

### Delegate-or-fallback ("one engine, one truth")

`graph-engine.mjs` mirrors the `/planr-pipeline:status` A.1/A.2 contract. When
the planr CLI is present and at version >= 1.7.2, the server shells out to
`planr graph --json` (or falls back to `planr status --json`). When the CLI is
absent or outdated, the native reader (`graph-reader.mjs`) does an equivalent
walk. Both paths validate against `schemas/v1.0.0/graph.schema.json`. A
conformance test asserts the two paths produce identical node sets on the shared
fixture in `conformance/fixtures/dashboard-graph/`. This means the dashboard and
`/status` can never diverge on the same project.

### Status classification

Node statuses are the same five values used by `/status`: `done`,
`in-progress`, `blocked`, `addressed`, `outstanding`. The mapping (in
`graph-reader.mjs:classifyStatus`) is:

- `done` — raw status is done, closed, completed, shipped, or released
- `addressed` — promoted or superseded
- `blocked` / `in-progress` — honoured verbatim from the raw frontmatter value
- everything else — `outstanding`

### Incremental SSE patches

The watcher does not push the full graph on every file change. It computes a
minimal diff (`diffGraphs`) between its last snapshot and the newly built graph,
and pushes only `{ updated, added, removed, edges }`. The client merges this in
place via `mergePatch()` in `main.js` without re-mounting any view, so the
selected node, active filters, zoom level, and scroll position are all preserved.

### Zero npm runtime dependencies

Every production file uses only Node stdlib and browser-native APIs. The client
app does not load any framework from a CDN. The graph layout engine
(`lib/dashboard/app/vendor/graph-layout.js`) is a self-contained vendored module,
not an npm package. The design-system stylesheet (`ds.css`) consumes tokens
from `.planr/design-system/tokens.css` — no external font or icon CDN.

### Shell and routing

The client app is a hash-routed single-page application. `main.js` calls
`hashRouter()` on every `hashchange` event, which dynamically imports
(`import('./views/<name>.js')`) the matching view module and calls its
`mount(contentEl)` function. The active module reference (`activeModule`) is
stored so that SSE patches can call `activeModule.partialRefresh(affectedIds)`
to repaint only changed nodes without remounting.

### Reuse-if-running

When `/planr-pipeline:dashboard` is called again, `dashboard-preflight.md` probes
`GET /health` on the existing port. If the response is `{ ok: true }`, the
running server is reused and `DASHBOARD_URL:` is printed immediately without
starting a second process. The PID file at
`<planrHome>/dashboard-daemon/<port>` is the discovery mechanism, shared with
the board daemon pattern from `lib/design-engine/daemon.mjs`.

## Dependencies on other features

| Feature | Usage |
|---------|-------|
| `lib/design-engine/daemon.mjs` | `writePidFile`, `readPidFile`, `isProcessAlive`, `isPortInUse` — shared server-lifecycle helpers |
| `.planr/design-system/tokens.css` | All 30 palette tokens; every hex value in `ds.css` must appear in this file (enforced by `verify-dashboard.mjs`) |
| `conformance/json-schema-validate.mjs` | Used by both `graph-reader.mjs` and `graph-engine.mjs` to validate the produced graph |
| `procedures/mode-detection.md` | Detects spec-driven vs default layout before the server reads any data |
| `commands/status.md` A.1/A.2 | The graph-engine's delegate-or-fallback pattern is a direct reuse of the `/status` data contract |

## Design-system wiring

The design system is enforced at three levels:

1. **CSS tokens** — `ds.css` imports from `.planr/design-system/tokens.css` at build time. All 541 CSS declarations use token variables; `verify-dashboard.mjs` confirms zero off-palette hex values in any scanned file.
2. **No raw hex in JS** — all eight view modules and the shell contain zero hex literals outside comments (confirmed by QA's Python-based scan).
3. **Lint gate** — `node lib/design/lint.mjs --expect-styles lib/dashboard/app/ds.css` exits clean (0 errors, 0 warnings).
